target_customer: Telecom operators, tower companies, real estate owners and local governments that acquire and manage infrastructure sites
problem: Acquiring sites for 5G masts and EV charging takes up to 24 months through manual, fragmented processes.
business_model: B2B SaaS platform for infrastructure site acquisition, project and asset management
product_category: Infrastructure asset and site management software

founders.name: Daniel Campion
previous_startups: Consulting and esports businesses (outcomes not stated)
founders.background_notes: YC page: strategy, M&A and capital projects in telecoms and infrastructure; board member of an oil and gas software firm acquired in 2021.

founders.name: Brian Sexton
founders.background_notes: YC page: technical leader building secure platforms, experience with SOC 2 and ISO 27001.

competitors.name: Accruent Siterra
competitors.what: Software for telecom site and lease management and site acquisition workflows
competitors.traction_then: Established product used by carriers; the dated source is a sponsored piece on an operator's implementation
competitors.funding_then: Owned by Accruent, not a venture-funded startup

technical_complexity.rationale: Workflow, mapping and data integration software across many stakeholders; standard SaaS engineering with some hard integration work.

defensibility.rationale: The YC page cites a UK government sponsored project with over 1 million assets on the platform and telecom players active, which creates data and workflow lock in, but the category had older incumbents.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No source shows an incumbent copying or buying Sitenna through 2025; partnerships with Hemphill, Palladin and Alpha Wireless were reported.

market_need_then: The company states site acquisition can take 24 months and that analysts expected a surge in 5G and EV charging deployments; no dated third party spend data was opened.

branding.domain_note: Uses sitenna.com, an exact match domain; acquisition history not found.

identity.visual_style: Product suite uses a consistent naming style (Prospect, Catalyst, Forge, Command, Spotlight, Nexus).

brand_strength.rationale: A niche B2B brand known mainly to telecom buyers; the sources show product naming discipline but no press about the brand itself.

outcome_analysis: Sitenna raised a 2.1 million dollar seed in early 2022 and about 3 million dollars in May 2023 to expand to the US, won a first US contract in late 2023, and added partnerships through 2025. Telecom industry founders with operator access gave it entry, and it remains active with modest disclosed funding. Whether it can scale past a niche enterprise market is not shown by the sources.
notes: The 2022 seed is reported by Silicon Republic, the Irish Times and a TotalTele press release (title seen only). The May 2023 round of 3M is from Silicon Republic; aggregators disagree on its label (seed or Series A) and on totals (3.53M SeedTable, 5.23M CB Insights), so stage is other. Sitetracker also offers site acquisition software but no dated source was found. The Samsung Next investment blog returned 404. The batch is Summer 2021; the YC page says founded 2020.
